Subset creation method for ExperimentSubset objects

Source: R/allGenerics.R, R/SubsetMethods.R
createSubset.Rd

Create a subset from an already available assay in the input ExperimentSubset object by specifying the rows and columns to include in the subset.

Usage

createSubset(
  x,
  subsetName,
  rows = NULL,
  cols = NULL,
  parentAssay = NULL,
  altExp = NULL
)

# S4 method for class 'SubsetSummarizedExperiment'
createSubset(x, subsetName, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, parentAssay = NULL, altExp = NULL)

# S4 method for class 'SubsetRangedSummarizedExperiment'
createSubset(x, subsetName, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, parentAssay = NULL, altExp = NULL)

# S4 method for class 'SubsetSingleCellExperiment'
createSubset(x, subsetName, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, parentAssay = NULL, altExp = NULL)

# S4 method for class 'SubsetTreeSummarizedExperiment'
createSubset(x, subsetName, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, parentAssay = NULL, altExp = NULL)

# S4 method for class 'SubsetSpatialExperiment'
createSubset(x, subsetName, rows = NULL, cols = NULL, parentAssay = NULL, altExp = NULL)

Arguments

x

ExperimentSubset Specify the object from which a subset should be created. Use ExperimentSubset() first to convert another experiment object.

subsetName

character(1) Specify the name of the subset to create.

rows

numeric or character vector. Specify the rows to include in this subset. If missing or NULL, all rows are included in the subset. Default NULL.

cols

numeric or character vector. Specify the columns to include in this subset. If missing or NULL, all columns are included in the subset. Default NULL.

parentAssay

character(1) Specify the parent assay of the subset: the name of a main assay, of a subset, or of an assay seen in a subset written as "subset/assay". If NULL, the first available main assay will be marked as parent. Default NULL. With altExp, it names an assay of that altExp instead; see the section below.

altExp

character(1) or NULL. The name of an alternative experiment (altExp) of the main object, such as "ADT", to make the subset from: rows then pick its features. Only for the classes that extend SingleCellExperiment. If NULL, the subset is made from the main object's features. Default NULL.

Value

An ExperimentSubset object that now contains the newly created subset.

Subsets made from an altExp

With altExp = "ADT", the subset's rows are features of the altExp "ADT", such as some of its proteins, and its columns are cells, as for any subset. parentAssay names an assay of the altExp, as the main object or a subset sees it:

  • NULL or "counts": the first assay, or the assay counts, of the main object's altExp. cols pick the main object's cells.

  • "clean" or "clean/clr": the first assay, or the assay clr, of the altExp as subset clean sees it, with the assays clean stores in it. cols pick clean's cells.

rows pick the altExp's features, by position or name. The subset sees every assay of the altExp as its parent does, linked and cut to its rows and cells, and stores its own with setSubsetAssay(), with the usual unlink rules. Its rowData with parentRowData = TRUE is the altExp's, and getSubsetExperiment() returns an object of the altExp's class. Subsets made from it, without altExp, pick its rows and cells. It doesn't see the main object's altExps. A row tree doesn't apply to it; column trees and spatial data are read at its cells.

Changes to the altExp carry along: renaming it, on the main object or in the subset it was made from, renames what the subset records; if it gets other rows, the subset keeps the features whose names remain; if it is removed, the subset and those made from it are dropped, with a warning. If the assay the subset was made from goes, it behaves as for a main assay: storing a subset's view of the altExp without that assay is an error, and a change to the main object's altExp that drops it leaves the subset without its parent assay.

Examples

data(sce_chcl, package = "scds")
es <- ExperimentSubset(sce_chcl)
es <- createSubset(es,
"subset1",
rows = c(10,11,50,56,98,99,102,105,109, 200),
cols = c(20,21,40,45,90,99,100,123,166,299),
parentAssay = "counts")
es
#> class: SubsetSingleCellExperiment 
#> dim: 2000 2000 
#> metadata(0):
#> assays(2): counts logcounts
#> rownames(2000): C12orf73 RNU6-1256P ... FOXF1 PRR3
#> rowData names(1): gene
#> colnames(2000): CTGCTGTCAGGGTATG CAGTCCTTCGGTTAAC ... GATGCTATCAGCAACT
#>   ATTTCTGGTGATGATA
#> colData names(11): nGene nUMI ... ident doublet_true_labels
#> reducedDimNames(0):
#> mainExpName: NULL
#> altExpNames(0):
#> subsets(1): subset1
#> subsetAssays(1): subset1

# an object with 10 genes and 20 cells
set.seed(1)
counts <- matrix(rpois(200, lambda = 5), nrow = 10)
rownames(counts) <- paste0("gene", 1:10)
colnames(counts) <- paste0("cell", 1:20)
es <- ExperimentSubset(list(counts = counts))
# counts of 4 proteins in the same cells, as the altExp "ADT"
adtCounts <- matrix(rpois(80, lambda = 20), nrow = 4)
rownames(adtCounts) <- c("CD3", "CD4", "CD8", "Isotype")
altExp(es, "ADT") <- SingleCellExperiment(list(counts = adtCounts))
#> Warning: 'colnames(value)' are not the same as 'colnames(x)' for 'altExp<-'.
#> This will be an error in the next release of Bioconductor.
# a subset of the first 12 cells
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "clean", cols = 1:12)
# a subset of clean's cells without the isotype control
es <- createSubset(es, subsetName = "clean.antibodies",
                   rows = c("CD3", "CD4", "CD8"),
                   parentAssay = "clean", altExp = "ADT")
dim(assay(es, "clean.antibodies"))
#> [1]  3 12
subsetParent(es, "clean.antibodies")
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "clean/ADT/counts"
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] "clean"
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [1] "counts"
#>
